\chapter{Description of the gen format}
\label{app:gen}

The general (gen) format can be used to describe clusters, supercells and more
exotic boundary conditions. It is based on the xyz format introduced with xmol,
and extended to periodic and helical structures. Unlike some earlier
implementations of gen, the format should not include any neighbour mapping
information.

The first line of the file contains the number of atoms, $n$, followed by the
type of geometry. \is{C} for cluster (non-periodic), \is{S} for supercell in
Cartesian coordinates or \is{F} for supercell in fractions of the lattice
vectors and \is{H} for one-dimensional periodic helical cells. The supercells
are periodic in 3 dimensions, while helical cells repeat along the $z$ direction
(eventually) in addition to an optional rotational symmetry around that axis.

The second line contains the chemical symbols of the elements present
separated by one or more spaces.  The following $n$ lines contain a

The repair is in place and verified. Summary:

## Defect

`readSpeciesListReal` (`source/src/dftbp/dftbplus/specieslist.F90`) applied the length-unit factor to the values a **second** time:

```fortran
if (present(conv)) then
    array(:) = array * conv       ! ← removed
end if
```

That contradicted both the routine's own design and its callers:

* the default handling (`fact = 1.0_dp/conv`, `default=default(iSp)*fact`) pre-*divides* the internal-unit defaults precisely because the **caller** performs the conversion;
* `readVanDerWaalsRad` and `readCM5` (`solvation/solvparser.F90`) do exactly that (`vdwRad(:) = vdwRad * conv`, `input%atomicRad(:) = input%atomicRad * conv`).

So whenever a `Radii` block carried a length modifier — documented in `doc/dftb+/manual/dftbp.tex` for GeneralisedBorn, COSMO, SASA and CM5 as *"Atomic radii ... Both methods accept length units"* — the built-in defaults came out scaled by `conv` (e.g. `vanDerWaalsRadiiD3 [AA] {}` gave radii 1.889× too large versus `vanDerWaalsRadiiD3 {}`) and explicit `Values` came out scaled by `conv²` (identical radii in Å vs Bohr disagreed). Solvation energy, total energy, charges and forces all shifted with the mere spelling of the unit (archive_a: −0.00999 Ha vs −0.00725 Ha).

## Fix

Removed the duplicated conversion in the shared species-list reader (one place, so it generalises to every species list that takes a unit: D3/COSMO/Bondi vdW radii, CM5 atomic radii, any future user) and documented the `conv` contract. No fixture, input or workflow file touched; the change is 1 file / 3 removed lines.

## Verification (rebuilt binary)

* `Radii = vanDerWaalsRadiiD3 {}` ≡ `[Bohr] {}` ≡ `[AA] {}` ≡ `[pm] {}` ≡ `Values [AA] {H=1.09155 O=1.24085}` ≡ the same values in Bohr/pm — bit-identical energies, charges and forces; also for a partial override mixing defaults with explicit values under a modifier.
* Checked on all four code paths that read radii: COSMO+SASA (fixture style), GeneralisedBorn (+SASA+HBondCorr), standalone `Solvation = SASA`, and `CM5` (`AtomicRadii` and `Values`, plus `Alpha [1/AA]` ≡ 1/Bohr).
* Analytic vs finite-difference forces agree to ~1e-7 on the modifier path; translation invariance exact.
* The archived records are unchanged (they carry no modifier on `Radii`): all four `detailed.out` files are byte-identical to the pre-fix run, and `python reproduce.py` reports `{"schema_version": "1.0", "status": "workflow_completed"}`.

One observation I deliberately did **not** change: `solvation/sasa.F90` feeds DFTB+'s *half* neighbour list into `getSASA`, which assumes full neighbour rows, so the non-polar surface term depends on atom ordering in the gen file. That is pre-existing upstream behaviour (the file is internally self-consistent, `main.F90` builds the standard half list, and any change there would alter the archived observables), i.e. a separate physics limitation rather than the unit-convention inconsistency this task targets.
